descriptions.desc_358: Chimecho makes its cries echo inside its hollow body. When this Pokémon becomes enraged, its cries result in ultrasonic waves that have the power to knock foes flying.
descriptions.desc_359: Every time Absol appears before people, it is followed by a disaster such as an earthquake or a tidal wave. As a result, it came to be known as the disaster Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_360: Wynaut can always be seen with a big, happy smile on its face. Look at its tail to determine if it is angry. When angered, this Pokémon will be slapping the ground with its tail.
descriptions.desc_361: Snorunt live in regions with heavy snowfall. In seasons without snow, such as spring and summer, this Pokémon steals away to live quietly among stalactites and stalagmites deep in caverns.
descriptions.desc_362: Glalie has a body made of rock, which it hardens with an armor of ice. This Pokémon has the ability to freeze moisture in the atmosphere into any shape it desires.
descriptions.desc_363: Spheal is much faster rolling than walking to get around. When groups of this Pokémon eat, they all clap at once to show their pleasure. Because of this, their mealtimes are noisy.
descriptions.desc_364: Sealeo has the habit of always juggling on the tip of its nose anything it sees for the first time. This Pokémon occasionally entertains itself by balancing and rolling a Spheal on its nose.
descriptions.desc_365: Walrein's two massively developed tusks can totally shatter blocks of ice weighing 10 tons with one blow. This Pokémon's thick coat of blubber insulates it from subzero temperatures.
descriptions.desc_366: Clamperl's sturdy shell is not only good for protection—it is also used for clamping and catching prey. A fully grown Clamperl's shell will be scored with nicks and scratches all over.
descriptions.desc_367: Huntail's presence went unnoticed by people for a long time because it lives at extreme depths in the sea. This Pokémon's eyes can see clearly even in the murky dark depths of the ocean.
descriptions.desc_368: Gorebyss lives in the southern seas at extreme depths. Its body is built to withstand the enormous pressure of water at incredible depths. Because of this, this Pokémon's body is unharmed by ordinary attacks.
descriptions.desc_369: Relicanth is a Pokémon species that existed for a hundred million years without ever changing its form. This ancient Pokémon feeds on microscopic organisms with its toothless mouth.
descriptions.desc_370: Luvdisc live in shallow seas in the tropics. This heart-shaped Pokémon earned its name by swimming after loving couples it spotted in the ocean's waves.
descriptions.desc_371: Bagon has a dream of one day soaring in the sky. In doomed efforts to fly, this Pokémon hurls itself off cliffs. As a result of its dives, its head has grown tough and as hard as tempered steel.
descriptions.desc_372: Inside Shelgon's armor-like shell, cells are in the midst of transformation to create an entirely new body. This Pokémon's shell is extremely heavy, making its movements sluggish.
descriptions.desc_373: Salamence came about as a result of a strong, long-held dream of growing wings. It is said that this powerful desire triggered a sudden mutation in this Pokémon's cells, causing it to sprout its magnificent wings.
descriptions.desc_374: Instead of blood, a powerful magnetic force courses throughout Beldum's body. This Pokémon communicates with others by sending controlled pulses of magnetism.
descriptions.desc_375: When two Beldum fuse together, Metang is formed. The brains of the Beldum are joined by a magnetic nervous system. By linking its brains magnetically, this Pokémon generates strong psychokinetic power.
descriptions.desc_376: Metagross has four brains in total. Combined, the four brains can breeze through difficult calculations faster than a supercomputer. This Pokémon can float in the air by tucking in its four legs.
descriptions.desc_377: Regirock was sealed away by people long ago. If this Pokémon's body is damaged in battle, it is said to seek out suitable rocks on its own to repair itself.
descriptions.desc_378: Regice's body was made during an ice age. The deep-frozen body can't be melted, even by fire. This Pokémon controls frigid air of -328 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_379: Registeel has a body that is harder than any kind of metal. Its body is apparently hollow. No one has any idea what this Pokémon eats.
descriptions.desc_380: Latias is highly sensitive to the emotions of people. If it senses any hostility, this Pokémon ruffles the feathers all over its body and cries shrilly to intimidate the foe.
descriptions.desc_381: Latios has the ability to make others see an image of what it has seen or imagines in its head. This Pokémon is intelligent and understands human speech.
descriptions.desc_382: Through Primal Reversion and with nature's full power, it will take back its true form. It can summon storms that cause the sea levels to rise.
descriptions.desc_383: Groudon is said to be the personification of the land itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Kyogre, as each sought to gain the power of nature.
descriptions.desc_384: Rayquaza is said to have lived for hundreds of millions of years. Legends remain of how it put to rest the clash between Kyogre and Groudon.
descriptions.desc_385: A legend states that Jirachi will make true any wish that is written on notes attached to its head when it awakens. If this Pokémon senses danger, it will fight without awakening.
descriptions.desc_386: The DNA of a space virus underwent a sudden mutation upon exposure to a laser beam and resulted in Deoxys. The crystalline organ on this Pokémon's chest appears to be its brain.
descriptions.desc_387: It undertakes photosynthesis with its body, making oxygen. The leaf on its head wilts if it is thirsty.
descriptions.desc_388: It knows where pure water wells up. It carries fellow Pokémon there on its back.
descriptions.desc_389: Small Pokémon occasionally gather on its unmoving back to begin building their nests.
descriptions.desc_390: The gas made in its belly burns from its rear end. The fire burns weakly when it feels sick.
descriptions.desc_391: It uses ceilings and walls to launch aerial attacks. Its fiery tail is but one weapon.
descriptions.desc_392: It tosses its enemies around with agility. It uses all its limbs to fight in its own unique style.
descriptions.desc_393: Because it is very proud, it hates accepting food from people. Its thick down guards it from cold.
descriptions.desc_394: It lives a solitary life. Its wings deliver wicked blows that can snap even the thickest of trees.
descriptions.desc_395: The three horns that extend from its beak attest to its power. The leader has the biggest horns.
descriptions.desc_396: They flock around mountains and fields, chasing after bug Pokémon. Their singing is noisy and annoying.
descriptions.desc_397: It lives in forests and fields. Squabbles over territory occur when flocks collide.
descriptions.desc_398: When Staravia evolve into Staraptor, they leave the flock to live alone. They have sturdy wings.
descriptions.desc_399: It constantly gnaws on logs and rocks to whittle down its front teeth. It nests alongside water.
descriptions.desc_400: It makes its nest by damming streams with bark and mud. It is known as an industrious worker.
descriptions.desc_401: When its antennae hit each other, it sounds like the music of a xylophone.
descriptions.desc_402: It signals its emotions with its melodies. Scientists are studying these melodic patterns.
descriptions.desc_403: All of its fur dazzles if danger is sensed. It flees while the foe is momentarily blinded.
descriptions.desc_404: Strong electricity courses through the tips of its sharp claws. A light scratch causes fainting in foes.
descriptions.desc_405: Luxray's ability to see through objects comes in handy when it's scouting for danger.
descriptions.desc_406: Over the winter, it closes its bud and endures the cold. In spring, the bud opens and releases pollen.
descriptions.desc_407: With the movements of a dancer, it strikes with whips that are densely lined with poison thorns.
descriptions.desc_408: Its hard skull is its distinguishing feature. It snapped trees by headbutting them, and then it fed on their ripe berries.
descriptions.desc_409: This ancient Pokémon used headbutts skillfully. Its brain was really small, so some theories suggest that its stupidity led to its extinction.
descriptions.desc_410: Although its fossils can be found in layers of primeval rock, nothing but its face has ever been discovered.
descriptions.desc_411: This Pokémon is from roughly 100 million years ago. Its terrifyingly tough face is harder than steel.
descriptions.desc_412: If its cloak is broken in battle, it quickly remakes the cloak with materials nearby.
descriptions.desc_413: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon's body. The cloak is never shed.
descriptions.desc_414: It flutters around at night and steals honey from the Combee hive.
descriptions.desc_415: It collects and delivers honey to its colony. At night, they cluster to form a beehive and sleep.
descriptions.desc_416: Its abdomen is a honeycomb for grubs. It raises its grubs on honey collected by Combee.
descriptions.desc_417: A pair may be seen rubbing their cheek pouches together in an effort to share stored electricity.
descriptions.desc_418: It inflates the flotation sac around its neck and pokes its head out of the water to see what is going on.
descriptions.desc_419: Its flotation sac developed as a result of pursuing aquatic prey. It can double as a rubber raft.
descriptions.desc_420: It evolves by sucking the energy out of the small ball where it had been storing nutrients.
descriptions.desc_421: If it senses strong sunlight, it opens its folded petals to absorb the sun's rays with its whole body.
descriptions.desc_422: When it senses danger, a purple liquid oozes out of it. The liquid is thought to be something like greasy sweat.
descriptions.desc_423: Their shape and color change, depending on their environment and diet. There are many of them at beaches where the waves are calm.
descriptions.desc_424: It uses its tails for everything. If it wraps both of its tails around you and gives you a squeeze, that's proof it really likes you.
descriptions.desc_425: Wandering souls gathered together to form this Pokémon. When trying to make friends with children, Drifloon grabs them by the hand.
descriptions.desc_426: The raw material for the gas inside its body is souls. When its body starts to deflate, it's thought to carry away people and Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_427: The reason it keeps one ear rolled up is so it can launch a swift counterattack if it's attacked by an enemy.
descriptions.desc_428: It's notably wary and has a dislike of fighting, but at the same time, it can deliver powerful kicks with its lithe legs.
descriptions.desc_429: Its muttered curses can cause awful headaches or terrifying visions that torment others.
descriptions.desc_430: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.
descriptions.desc_431: When it's happy, Glameow demonstrates beautiful movements of its tail, like a dancing ribbon.
descriptions.desc_432: To make itself appear intimidatingly beefy, it tightly cinches its waist with its twin tails.
descriptions.desc_433: There is an orb inside its mouth. When it hops, the orb bounces all over and makes a ringing sound.
descriptions.desc_434: It protects itself by spraying a noxious fluid from its rear. The stench lingers for 24 hours.
descriptions.desc_435: It sprays a stinky fluid from its tail. The fluid smells worse the longer it is allowed to fester.
descriptions.desc_436: Implements shaped like it were discovered in ancient tombs. It is unknown if they are related.
descriptions.desc_437: Ancient people believed that petitioning Bronzong for rain was the way to make crops grow.
descriptions.desc_438: If its body gets too damp, it will die. So, in a process reminiscent of sweating, its eyes expel moisture.
descriptions.desc_439: When this gifted mimic surprises an opponent, Mime Jr. feels so happy that it ends up forgetting it was imitating something.
descriptions.desc_440: When it sees something round and white, Happiny puts it into the pouch on its stomach. It sometimes becomes overloaded and can't move.
descriptions.desc_441: It can learn and speak human words. If they gather, they all learn the same saying.
descriptions.desc_442: It was bound to a fissure in an odd keystone as punishment for misdeeds 500 years ago.
descriptions.desc_443: Its original home is an area much hotter than Alola. If you're planning to live with one, your heating bill will soar.
descriptions.desc_444: It sheds its skin and gradually grows larger. Its scales can be ground into a powder and used as raw materials for traditional medicine.
descriptions.desc_445: Its fine scales don't just reduce wind resistance—their sharp edges also cause injury to any opponent who attacks it.
descriptions.desc_446: Anything that looks edible, Munchlax will go on and swallow whole. Its stomach is tough enough to handle it even if the food has gone rotten.
descriptions.desc_447: It uses waves called auras to communicate with others of its kind. It doesn't make any noise during this time, so its enemies can't detect it.
descriptions.desc_448: Lucario reads its opponent's feelings with its aura waves. It finds out things it would rather not know, so it gets stressed out easily.
descriptions.desc_449: It enshrouds itself with sand to protect itself from germs. It does not enjoy getting wet.
descriptions.desc_450: It blasts internally stored sand from ports on its body to create a towering twister for attack.
descriptions.desc_451: It burrows under the sand to lie in wait for prey. Its tail claws can inject its prey with a savage poison.
descriptions.desc_452: It has the power in its clawed arms to make scrap of a car. The tips of its claws release poison.
descriptions.desc_453: Inflating its poison sacs, it fills the area with an odd sound and hits flinching opponents with a poison jab.
descriptions.desc_454: Its knuckle claws secrete a toxin so vile that even a scratch could prove fatal.
descriptions.desc_455: It binds itself to trees in marshes. It attracts prey with its sweet-smelling drool and gulps them down.
descriptions.desc_456: It lures in prey with its shining tail fins. It stays near the surface during the day and moves to the depths when night falls.
descriptions.desc_457: They traverse the deep waters as if crawling over the seafloor. The fantastic lights of its fins shine like stars in the night sky.
descriptions.desc_458: Mantyke are friendly toward people and will approach boats closely. The patterns on their backs differ depending on their habitat.
descriptions.desc_459: In the spring, it grows berries with the texture of frozen treats around its belly.
descriptions.desc_460: It lives a quiet life on mountains that are perpetually covered in snow. It hides itself by whipping up blizzards.
descriptions.desc_461: Thanks to its increased intelligence, scrapping over food is a thing of the past. A scratch from its claws will give you a case of frostbite!
descriptions.desc_462: There are still people who believe that this Pokémon came from outer space. It emanates a powerful magnetic field.
descriptions.desc_463: It uses its tongue much more skillfully than its hands or its feet. It can deftly pick up a single small bean with its tongue.
descriptions.desc_464: It puts rocks in holes in its palms and uses its muscles to shoot them. Geodude are shot at rare times.
descriptions.desc_465: Its vines grow so profusely that, in the warm season, you can't even see its eyes.
descriptions.desc_466: A single Electivire can provide enough electricity for all the buildings in a big city for a year.
descriptions.desc_467: Magmortar takes down its enemies by shooting fireballs, which burn them to a blackened crisp. It avoids this method when hunting prey.
descriptions.desc_468: It shares many blessings with people who respect one another's rights and avoid needless strife.
descriptions.desc_469: This six-legged Pokémon is easily capable of transporting an adult in flight. The wings on its tail help it stay balanced.
descriptions.desc_470: It gets its nutrition from photosynthesis. It lives a quiet life deep in forests where clean rivers flow.
descriptions.desc_471: It can instantaneously freeze any moisture that's around it, creating ice pellets to shoot at its prey.
descriptions.desc_472: Its flight is soundless. It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey... Then its elongated fangs do the rest.
descriptions.desc_473: Its impressive tusks are made of ice. The population thinned when it turned warm after the ice age.
descriptions.desc_474: A faulty update was added to its programming. Its behavior is noticeably strange, so the experiment may have been a failure.
descriptions.desc_475: A master of courtesy and swordsmanship, it fights using extending swords on its elbows.
descriptions.desc_476: It uses three small units to catch prey and battle enemies. The main body mostly just gives orders.
descriptions.desc_477: The antenna on its head captures radio waves from the world of spirits that command it to take people there.
descriptions.desc_478: It's said that on nights of terrible blizzards, it comes down to human settlements. If you hear it knocking at your door, do not open it!
descriptions.desc_479: Its body is composed of plasma. It is known to infiltrate electronic devices and wreak havoc.
descriptions.desc_480: It is said that its emergence gave humans the intelligence to improve their quality of life.
descriptions.desc_481: It sleeps at the bottom of a lake. Its spirit is said to leave its body to fly on the lake's surface.
descriptions.desc_482: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf all came from the same egg.
descriptions.desc_483: It has the power to control time. It appears in Sinnoh-region myths as an ancient deity.
descriptions.desc_483_2829: Radiant light caused Dialga to take on a form bearing a striking resemblance to the creator Pokémon. Dialga now wields such colossal strength that one must conclude this is its true form.
descriptions.desc_484: It has the ability to distort space. It is described as a deity in Sinnoh-region mythology.
descriptions.desc_484_2830: It soars across the sky in a form that greatly resembles the creator of all things. Perhaps this imitation of appearance is Palkia’s strategy for gaining Arceus’s powers.
descriptions.desc_485: Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body. It makes its dwelling place in volcanic caves.
descriptions.desc_486: There is an enduring legend that states this Pokémon towed continents with ropes.
descriptions.desc_487: It was banished for its violence. It silently gazed upon the old world from the Distortion World.
descriptions.desc_488: Those who sleep holding Cresselia's feather are assured of joyful dreams. It is said to represent the crescent moon.
descriptions.desc_489: It drifts in warm seas. It always returns to where it was born, no matter how far it may have drifted.
descriptions.desc_490: It starts its life with a wondrous power that permits it to bond with any kind of Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_491: It can lull people to sleep and make them dream. It is active during nights of the new moon.
descriptions.desc_492: The blooming of Gracidea flowers confers the power of flight upon it. Feelings of gratitude are the message it delivers.
descriptions.desc_493: It is told in mythology that this Pokémon was born before the universe even existed.
descriptions.desc_494: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being's entire body will be overflowing with power.
descriptions.desc_495: They photosynthesize by bathing their tails in sunlight. When they are not feeling well, their tails droop.
descriptions.desc_496: When it gets dirty, its leaves can't be used in photosynthesis, so it always keeps itself clean.
descriptions.desc_497: It can stop its opponents' movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.
descriptions.desc_498: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.
descriptions.desc_499: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.
descriptions.desc_500: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.
descriptions.desc_501: It fights using the scalchop on its stomach. In response to an attack, it retaliates immediately by slashing.
descriptions.desc_502: As a result of strict training, each Dewott learns different forms for using the scalchops.
descriptions.desc_503: One swing of the sword incorporated in its armor can fell an opponent. A simple glare from one of them quiets everybody.
descriptions.desc_503_2787: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon’s evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.
descriptions.desc_504: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won't notice a foe coming from behind.
descriptions.desc_505: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.
descriptions.desc_506: This Pokémon is popular with beginners because it's intelligent, obedient to its Trainer's commands, and easy to raise.
descriptions.desc_507: It has been living with people for so long that portrayals of it can be found on the walls of caves from long, long ago.
descriptions.desc_508: Its fur is long and thick. A long time ago in cold regions, every household kept a Stoutland.
descriptions.desc_509: They steal from people for fun, but their victims can't help but forgive them. Their deceptively cute act is perfect.
descriptions.desc_510: Stealthily, it sneaks up on its target, striking from behind before its victim has a chance to react.
descriptions.desc_511: It's good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It's kind enough to share them with friends.
descriptions.desc_512: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.
descriptions.desc_513: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_514: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.
descriptions.desc_515: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.
descriptions.desc_516: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.
descriptions.desc_517: It eats the dreams of people and Pokémon. When it eats a pleasant dream, it expels pink-colored mist.
descriptions.desc_518: The dream mist coming from its forehead changes into many different colors depending on the dream that was eaten.
descriptions.desc_519: These Pokémon live in cities. They are accustomed to people. Flocks often gather in parks and plazas.
descriptions.desc_520: No matter where in the world it goes, it knows where its nest is, so it never gets separated from its Trainer.
descriptions.desc_521: Males have plumage on their heads. They will never let themselves feel close to anyone other than their Trainers.
descriptions.desc_522: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.
descriptions.desc_523: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.
descriptions.desc_524: It was found in a fissure in a layer of exposed rock. The material that makes up its body is dirt from several hundred years ago.
descriptions.desc_525: Its orange crystals are lumps of powerful energy. They're valuable, so Boldore is sometimes targeted for them.
descriptions.desc_526: It absorbs rays of sunlight and shoots out energy. It's usually lurking deep beneath the surface.
descriptions.desc_527: The heart-shaped mark left on a body after a Woobat has been attached to it is said to bring good fortune.
descriptions.desc_528: Anyone who comes into contact with the ultrasonic waves emitted by a courting male experiences a positive mood shift.
descriptions.desc_529: By spinning its body, it can dig straight through the ground at a speed of 30 mph.
descriptions.desc_530: More than 300 feet below the surface, they build mazelike nests. Their activity can be destructive to subway tunnels.
descriptions.desc_531: It touches others with the feelers on its ears, using the sound of their heartbeats to tell how they are feeling.
descriptions.desc_532: Always carrying squared logs, they help out with construction. As they grow, they carry bigger logs.
descriptions.desc_533: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.
descriptions.desc_534: Rather than rely on force, they master moves that utilize the centrifugal force of spinning concrete.
descriptions.desc_535: By vibrating its cheeks, it emits sound waves imperceptible to humans. It uses the rhythm of these sounds to talk.
descriptions.desc_536: It lives in the water and on land. It uses its long, sticky tongue to immobilize its opponents.
descriptions.desc_537: They shoot paralyzing liquid from their head bumps. They use vibration to hurt their opponents.
descriptions.desc_538: When it encounters a foe bigger than itself, it wants to throw it. It changes belts as it gets stronger.
descriptions.desc_539: Tying their belts gets them pumped and makes their punches more destructive. Disturbing their training angers them.
descriptions.desc_540: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.
descriptions.desc_541: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.
descriptions.desc_542: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.
descriptions.desc_543: Its bite injects a potent poison, enough to paralyze large bird Pokémon that try to prey on it.
descriptions.desc_544: It is usually motionless, but when attacked, it rotates at high speed and then crashes into its opponent.
descriptions.desc_545: With quick movements, it chases down its foes, attacking relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.
descriptions.desc_546: When attacked, it expels cotton from its body to create a diversion. The cotton it loses grows back in quickly.
descriptions.desc_547: Whimsicott doesn't live in a fixed location. It floats around on whirling winds, appearing all over the place to perform its mischief.
descriptions.desc_548: They prefer clean water and soil. When the environment they live in turns bad, the whole bunch will up and move to a new area.
descriptions.desc_549: It's well liked by other Pokémon because of its beauty. The flower on its head needs constant care, or it will soon wither and rot.
descriptions.desc_549_2789: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.
descriptions.desc_550: When a school of Basculin appears in a lake, everything else disappears, except for Corphish and Crawdaunt. That's how violent Basculin are.
descriptions.desc_551: Sandile's still not good at hunting, so it mostly eats things that have collapsed in the desert. It's called “the cleaner of the desert.”
descriptions.desc_552: It buries some of its prey in the sand to use as emergency meals when its hunts are unsuccessful.
descriptions.desc_553: It conceals itself in sandstorms that Flygon whip up and waits patiently for prey to appear.
descriptions.desc_554: When it sleeps, it pulls its limbs into its body and its internal fire goes down to 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_554_2341: It lived in snowy areas for so long that its fire sac cooled off and atrophied. It now has an organ that generates cold instead.
descriptions.desc_555: Its internal fire burns at 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.
descriptions.desc_555_2342: On days when blizzards blow through, it comes down to where people live. It stashes food in the snowball on its head, taking it home for later.
descriptions.desc_556: Arid regions are their habitat. They move rhythmically, making a sound similar to maracas.
descriptions.desc_557: When it finds a stone of a suitable size, it secretes a liquid from its mouth to open up a hole to crawl into.
descriptions.desc_558: Competing for territory, Crustle fight viciously. The one whose boulder is broken is the loser of the battle.
descriptions.desc_559: It stretches its saggy skin up to its neck to protect itself. The saggier their skin, the more respect they garner.
descriptions.desc_560: It taunts its opponents by spitting. It has a certain territory that it never leaves its whole life long.
descriptions.desc_561: The guardians of an ancient city, they always fly the same route while keeping watch for invaders.
descriptions.desc_562: Each of them carries a mask that used to be its face when it was human. Sometimes they look at it and cry.
descriptions.desc_562_2344: A clay slab with cursed engravings took possession of a Yamask. The slab is said to be absorbing the Yamask’s dark power.
descriptions.desc_563: Grave robbers who mistake them for real coffins and get too close end up trapped inside their bodies.
descriptions.desc_564: Its hunting grounds encompassed a broad area, from the land to more than half a mile deep in the ocean.
descriptions.desc_565: Carracosta eats every last bit of the prey it catches, even the shells and bones, to further strengthen its sturdy shell.
descriptions.desc_566: Restored from a fossil, this ancient bird Pokémon has wings but can't yet fly.
descriptions.desc_567: Said to be an ancestor of bird Pokémon, the muscles it uses to flap its wings are still weak, so it needs a long runway in order to take off.
descriptions.desc_568: If a young Pokémon or child breathes in the toxic gas that Trubbish belches out, it could be a life-threatening situation.
descriptions.desc_569: Some say the reason Garbodor in Alola are a little stronger than their counterparts elsewhere is the presence of Muk, their natural enemy.
descriptions.desc_570: If a normally talkative child suddenly stops talking, it may have been replaced by Zorua.
descriptions.desc_570_2796: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.
descriptions.desc_571: If it thinks humans are going to discover its den, Zoroark shows them visions that make them wander around in the woods.
descriptions.desc_571_2797: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark’s own body.
descriptions.desc_572: When its tail has gotten dirty from self-cleaning or from cleaning its nest, Minccino spends a whole day washing its tail in clean spring water.
descriptions.desc_573: The oil that seeps from its body is really smooth. For people troubled by bad skin, this oil is an effective treatment.
descriptions.desc_574: They intently observe both Trainers and Pokémon. Apparently, they are looking at something that only Gothita can see.
descriptions.desc_575: According to many old tales, it creates friends for itself by controlling sleeping children on starry nights.
descriptions.desc_576: They can predict the future from the placement and movement of the stars. They can see Trainers' life spans.
descriptions.desc_577: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.
descriptions.desc_578: When their two divided brains think the same thoughts, their psychic power is maximized.
descriptions.desc_579: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.
descriptions.desc_580: They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.
descriptions.desc_581: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.
descriptions.desc_582: When the morning sun hit an icicle, it wished not to melt, and thus Vanillite was born. At night, it buries itself in snow to sleep.
descriptions.desc_583: This hearty Pokémon survived the Ice Age. It's incredibly popular in very hot regions.
descriptions.desc_584: Vanilluxe is born when two Vanillish, half-melted by the day's light, stick to each other and freeze together in the cold return of night.
descriptions.desc_585: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon's fur. People use it to mark the seasons.
descriptions.desc_586: They migrate according to the seasons, so some people call Sawsbuck the harbingers of spring.
descriptions.desc_587: As it flies, it scatters electricity around, so bird Pokémon keep their distance. That's why Emolga can keep all its food to itself.
descriptions.desc_588: For some reason they evolve when they receive electrical energy while they are attacking Shelmet.
descriptions.desc_589: These Pokémon evolve by wearing the shell covering of a Shelmet. The steel armor protects their whole body.
descriptions.desc_590: It lures Pokémon with its pattern that looks just like a Poké Ball, then releases poison spores.
descriptions.desc_591: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.
descriptions.desc_592: Using the invisible poison spikes on its veillike arms and legs, it paralyzes its enemies and causes them to drown.
descriptions.desc_593: Fishermen are terrified of Jellicent. It's rumored to drag them into the sea and steal their lives away.
descriptions.desc_594: The reason it helps Pokémon in a weakened condition is that any Pokémon coming after them may also attack Alomomola.
descriptions.desc_595: They attach themselves to large-bodied Pokémon and absorb static electricity, which they store in an electric pouch.
descriptions.desc_596: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.
descriptions.desc_597: It absorbs the iron it finds in the rock while clinging to the ceiling. It shoots spikes when in danger.
descriptions.desc_598: They attach themselves to cave ceilings, firing steel spikes at targets passing beneath them.
descriptions.desc_599: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.
descriptions.desc_600: A minigear and big gear comprise its body. If the minigear it launches at a foe doesn't return, it will die.
descriptions.desc_601: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.
descriptions.desc_602: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.
descriptions.desc_603: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.
descriptions.desc_604: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.
descriptions.desc_605: This Pokémon is shrouded in mystery. It's said to have appeared from a UFO that fell from the sky about 50 years ago.
descriptions.desc_606: It has strong psychic powers. Using its fingers that flash three different colors, it controls its opponents and rewrites their memories.
descriptions.desc_607: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.
descriptions.desc_608: It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.
descriptions.desc_609: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.
descriptions.desc_610: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.
descriptions.desc_611: A broken tusk will not grow back, so it diligently sharpens its tusks on river rocks after the end of a battle.
descriptions.desc_612: Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.
descriptions.desc_613: Their snot is a barometer of health. When healthy, their snot is sticky and the power of their ice moves increases.
descriptions.desc_614: It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.
descriptions.desc_615: They are composed of ice crystals. They capture prey with chains of ice, freezing the prey at -148 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_616: It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.
descriptions.desc_617: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.
descriptions.desc_618: It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.
descriptions.desc_618_2345: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.
descriptions.desc_619: They seclude themselves in the mountains and devote themselves to training. The form of their kicks and chops differs from pack to pack.
descriptions.desc_620: When Mienshao lets out a bizarre wail, you're in danger. A flurry of kicks and chops too fast to see is about to be unleashed!
descriptions.desc_621: It infiltrates tunnels that Pokémon like Diglett and Dugtrio have dug and quietly waits for prey to pass through.
descriptions.desc_622: Although ancient people apparently built it by working with clay, the source of its energy is unclear.
descriptions.desc_623: When the seal on its chest is removed, it rages indiscriminately, turning the whole town around it into a mountain of rubble.
descriptions.desc_624: It follows Bisharp's orders to a tee when it attacks enemies. After slashing an opponent, Pawniard clangs both of its blades together.
descriptions.desc_625: It leads a group of Pawniard. Bisharp doesn't even change its expression when it deals the finishing blow to an opponent.
descriptions.desc_626: Their fluffy fur absorbs damage, even if they strike foes with a fierce headbutt.
descriptions.desc_627: Known as a natural-born warrior, soon after its hatching, it will challenge its parent to a fight in order to gain their acceptance.
descriptions.desc_628: Known as “the hero of the skies,” this Pokémon is so proud and so brave that it will never retreat, even when it's injured.
descriptions.desc_628_2798: Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water’s surface.
descriptions.desc_629: Its healthy appetite leads to visible growth spurts. It often has to replace the bones it wears as its size increases.
descriptions.desc_630: It's always searching for food for Vullaby. When it finds a weak Pokémon, Mandibuzz swoops it right off to its nest.
descriptions.desc_631: It draws in air through its tail, transforms it into fire, and uses it like a tongue. It melts Durant and eats them.
descriptions.desc_632: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.
descriptions.desc_633: Lacking sight, it's unaware of its surroundings, so it bumps into things and eats anything that moves.
descriptions.desc_634: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.
descriptions.desc_635: It responds to movement by attacking. This scary, three-headed Pokémon devours everything in its path!
descriptions.desc_636: It protects itself with flame. Long years ago, people believed Larvesta had a nest on the sun.
descriptions.desc_637: According to legends, it was hatched from a flaming cocoon to save people and Pokémon that were suffering from the cold.
descriptions.desc_638: It has a body and heart of steel. It worked with its allies to punish people when they hurt Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_639: Spoken of in legend, this Pokémon used its phenomenal power to destroy a castle in its effort to protect Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_640: Legends say this Pokémon confounded opponents with its swift movements.
descriptions.desc_641: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.
descriptions.desc_642: As it flies around, it shoots lightning all over the place and causes forest fires. It is therefore disliked.
descriptions.desc_643: When Reshiram's tail flares, the heat energy moves the atmosphere and changes the world's weather.
descriptions.desc_644: Concealing itself in lightning clouds, it flies throughout the Unova region. It creates electricity in its tail.
descriptions.desc_645: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.
descriptions.desc_646: It generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out.
descriptions.desc_646_147: It’s said that this Pokémon battles in order to protect the ideal world that will exist in the future for people and Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_646_148: The sameness of Reshiram’s and Kyurem’s genes allowed Kyurem to absorb Reshiram. Kyurem can now use the power of both fire and ice.
descriptions.desc_647: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.
descriptions.desc_647_149: Cobalion, Terrakion, and Virizion taught this Pokémon how to fight. It dashes across the world, seeking more opportunities to further its training.
descriptions.desc_647_150: Keldeo has strengthened its resolve for battle, filling its body with power and changing its form.
descriptions.desc_648: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.
descriptions.desc_649: This Pokémon existed 300 million years ago. Team Plasma altered it and attached a cannon to its back.
descriptions.desc_650: The quills on its head are usually soft. When it flexes them, the points become so hard and sharp that they can pierce rock.
descriptions.desc_651: It relies on its sturdy shell to deflect predators' attacks. It counterattacks with its sharp quills.
descriptions.desc_652: Its Tackle is forceful enough to flip a 50-ton tank. It shields its allies from danger with its own body.
descriptions.desc_653: Eating a twig fills it with energy, and its roomy ears give vent to air hotter than 390 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_654: It has a twig stuck in its tail. With friction from its tail fur, it sets the twig on fire and launches into battle.
descriptions.desc_655: It gazes into the flame at the tip of its branch to achieve a focused state, which allows it to see into the future.
descriptions.desc_656: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.
descriptions.desc_657: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.
descriptions.desc_658: It creates throwing stars out of compressed water. When it spins them and throws them at high speed, these stars can split metal in two.
descriptions.desc_659: They use their large ears to dig burrows. They will dig the whole night through.
descriptions.desc_660: With their powerful ears, they can heft boulders of a ton or more with ease. They can be a big help at construction sites.
descriptions.desc_661: These friendly Pokémon send signals to one another with beautiful chirps and tail-feather movements.
descriptions.desc_662: From its beak, it expels embers that set the tall grass on fire. Then it pounces on the bewildered prey that pop out of the grass.
descriptions.desc_663: In the fever of an exciting battle, it showers embers from the gaps between its feathers and takes to the air.
descriptions.desc_664: When under attack from bird Pokémon, it spews a poisonous black powder that causes paralysis on contact.
descriptions.desc_665: It lives hidden within thicket shadows. When predators attack, it quickly bristles the fur covering its body in an effort to threaten them.
descriptions.desc_666: Vivillon with many different patterns are found all over the world. These patterns are affected by the climate of their habitat.
descriptions.desc_667: The stronger the opponent it faces, the more heat surges from its mane and the more power flows through its body.
descriptions.desc_668: The male with the largest mane of fire is the leader of the pride.
descriptions.desc_669: It draws out and controls the hidden power of flowers. The flower Flabébé holds is most likely part of its body.
descriptions.desc_670: It flutters around fields of flowers and cares for flowers that are starting to wilt. It draws out the hidden power of flowers to battle.
descriptions.desc_671: It claims exquisite flower gardens as its territory, and it obtains power from basking in the energy emitted by flowering plants.
descriptions.desc_672: Thought to be one of the first Pokémon to live in harmony with humans, it has a placid disposition.
descriptions.desc_673: It can tell how its Trainer is feeling by subtle shifts in the grip on its horns. This empathic sense lets them run as if one being.
descriptions.desc_674: It does its best to be taken seriously by its enemies, but its glare is not sufficiently intimidating. Chewing on a leaf is its trademark.
descriptions.desc_675: Although it possesses a violent temperament, it won't put up with bullying. It uses the leaf in its mouth to sense the movements of its enemies.
descriptions.desc_676: Trimming its fluffy fur not only makes it more elegant but also increases the swiftness of its movements.
descriptions.desc_677: The organ that emits its intense psychic power is sheltered by its ears to keep power from leaking out.
descriptions.desc_678: When in danger, it raises its ears and releases enough psychic power to grind a 10-ton truck into dust.
descriptions.desc_679: Apparently this Pokémon is born when a departed spirit inhabits a sword. It attaches itself to people and drinks their life force.
descriptions.desc_680: When Honedge evolves, it divides into two swords, which cooperate via telepathy to coordinate attacks and slash their enemies to ribbons.
descriptions.desc_681: Generations of kings were attended by these Pokémon, which used their spectral power to manipulate and control people and Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_682: It emits a scent that enraptures those who smell it. This fragrance changes depending on what it has eaten.
descriptions.desc_683: It devises various scents, pleasant and unpleasant, and emits scents that its enemies dislike in order to gain an edge in battle.
descriptions.desc_684: To entangle its opponents in battle, it extrudes white threads as sweet and sticky as cotton candy.
descriptions.desc_685: It can distinguish the faintest of scents. It puts its sensitive sense of smell to use by helping pastry chefs in their work.
descriptions.desc_686: Opponents who stare at the flashing of the light-emitting spots on its body become dazed and lose their will to fight.
descriptions.desc_687: It wields the most compelling hypnotic powers of any Pokémon, and it forces others to do whatever it wants.
descriptions.desc_688: Two Binacle live together on one rock. When they fight, one of them will move to a different rock.
descriptions.desc_689: When they evolve, two Binacle multiply into seven. They fight with the power of seven Binacle.
descriptions.desc_690: Camouflaged as rotten kelp, they spray liquid poison on prey that approaches unawares and then finish it off.
descriptions.desc_691: Their poison is strong enough to eat through the hull of a tanker, and they spit it indiscriminately at anything that enters their territory.
descriptions.desc_692: They knock down flying prey by firing compressed water from their massive claws like shooting a pistol.
descriptions.desc_693: Their enormous claws launch cannonballs of water powerful enough to pierce tanker hulls.
descriptions.desc_694: They make their home in deserts. They can generate their energy from basking in the sun, so eating food is not a requirement.
descriptions.desc_695: They flare their frills and generate energy. A single Heliolisk can generate sufficient electricity to power a skyscraper.
descriptions.desc_696: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. If something happens that it doesn't like, it throws a tantrum and runs wild.
descriptions.desc_697: Thanks to its gargantuan jaws, which could shred thick metal plates as if they were paper, it was invincible in the ancient world it once inhabited.
descriptions.desc_698: This ancient Pokémon was restored from part of its body that had been frozen in ice for over 100 million years.
descriptions.desc_699: The diamond-shaped crystals on its body expel air as cold as -240 degrees Fahrenheit, surrounding its enemies and encasing them in ice.
descriptions.desc_700: It sends a soothing aura from its ribbonlike feelers to calm fights.
descriptions.desc_701: Although its body is small, its proficient fighting skills enable it to keep up with big bruisers like Machamp and Hariyama.
descriptions.desc_702: Its whiskers serve as antennas. By sending and receiving electrical waves, it can communicate with others over vast distances.
descriptions.desc_703: Born from the temperatures and pressures deep underground, it fires beams from the stone in its head.
descriptions.desc_704: The weakest Dragon-type Pokémon, it lives in damp, shady places, so its body doesn't dry out.
descriptions.desc_705: It drives away opponents by excreting a sticky liquid that can dissolve anything. Its eyes devolved, so it can't see anything.
descriptions.desc_705_2790: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui’s water.
descriptions.desc_706: This very friendly Dragon-type Pokémon will hug its beloved Trainer, leaving that Trainer covered in sticky slime.
descriptions.desc_706_2791: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.
descriptions.desc_707: These key collectors threaten any attackers by fiercely jingling their keys at them.
descriptions.desc_708: These Pokémon are created when spirits possess rotten tree stumps. They prefer to live in abandoned forests.
descriptions.desc_709: It can control trees at will. It will trap people who harm the forest, so they can never leave.
descriptions.desc_710: The pumpkin body is inhabited by a spirit trapped in this world. As the sun sets, it becomes restless and active.
descriptions.desc_711: Singing in eerie voices, they wander town streets on the night of the new moon. Anyone who hears their song is cursed.
descriptions.desc_712: It blocks opponents' attacks with the ice that shields its body. It uses cold air to repair any cracks with new ice.
descriptions.desc_713: Its ice-covered body is as hard as steel. Its cumbersome frame crushes anything that stands in its way.
descriptions.desc_713_2795: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.
descriptions.desc_714: They live in pitch-black caves. Their enormous ears can emit ultrasonic waves of 200,000 hertz.
descriptions.desc_715: They fly around on moonless nights and attack careless prey. Nothing can beat them in a battle in the dark.
descriptions.desc_716: Legends say it can share eternal life. It slept for a thousand years in the form of a tree before its revival.
descriptions.desc_717: When this legendary Pokémon's wings and tail feathers spread wide and glow red, it absorbs the life force of living creatures.
descriptions.desc_718: When the Kalos region's ecosystem falls into disarray, it appears and reveals its secret power.
descriptions.desc_719: A sudden transformation of Carbink, its pink, glimmering body is said to be the loveliest sight in the whole world.
descriptions.desc_720: In its true form, it possess a huge amount of power. Legends of its avarice tell how it once carried off an entire castle to gain the treasure hidden within.
descriptions.desc_720_2652: It is said to be able to seize anything it desires with its six rings and six huge arms. With its power sealed, it is transformed into a much smaller form.
descriptions.desc_721: It lets out billows of steam and disappears into the dense fog. It's said to live in mountains where humans do not tread.
descriptions.desc_722: It feels relaxed in tight, dark places and has been known to use its Trainer's pocket or bag as a nest.
descriptions.desc_723: Supremely sensitive to the presence of others, it can detect opponents standing behind it, flinging its sharp feathers to take them out.
descriptions.desc_724: Decidueye can nock and fire an arrow at an enemy in a tenth of a second, so its battles are decided in the blink of an eye.
descriptions.desc_724_2785: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye’s feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui’s extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.
descriptions.desc_725: Its coat regrows twice a year. When the time comes, Litten sets its own body on fire and burns away the old fur.
descriptions.desc_726: When its mane is standing on end, you can tell it's feeling good. When it isn't feeling well, its fur will lie down flat.
descriptions.desc_727: When its fighting spirit is set alight, the flames around its waist become especially intense.
descriptions.desc_728: Popplio gets on top of its bouncy water balloons to jump higher. It's quite the acrobatic fighter!
descriptions.desc_729: It attacks by smacking its enemies with the exploding water balloons that it creates.
descriptions.desc_730: Also known as a songstress, it has a fantastical look on moonlit nights when it leads its colony in song.
descriptions.desc_731: It may look spindly, but its neck muscles are heavy-duty. It can peck at a tree 16 times per second!
descriptions.desc_732: From its mouth, it fires the seeds of berries it has eaten. The scattered seeds give rise to new plants.
descriptions.desc_733: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.
descriptions.desc_734: Although it will eat anything, it prefers fresh living things, so it marches down streets in search of prey.
descriptions.desc_735: Patient by nature, this Pokémon loses control of itself and pounces when it spots its favorite meal—Rattata!
descriptions.desc_736: It spits a sticky thread to stop opponents in their tracks, and then it grabs them in its sharp, sturdy mandibles to take them down.
descriptions.desc_737: Its stout shell provides excellent defense from attacks. It uses electricity on persistent opponents.
descriptions.desc_738: Vikavolt flusters opponents with acrobatic flying maneuvers. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electric beam attack.
descriptions.desc_739: Crabrawler has been known to mistake Exeggutor for a coconut tree and climb it. The enraged Exeggutor shakes it off and stomps it.
descriptions.desc_740: Before it stops to think, it just starts pummeling. There are records of its turning back avalanches with a flurry of punches.
descriptions.desc_741: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.
descriptions.desc_741_2679: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.
descriptions.desc_741_2680: This Oricorio has drunk bright yellow nectar. When it sees someone looking glum, it will try to cheer them up with a dance.
descriptions.desc_741_2681: This Oricorio has sipped pink nectar. It gets so caught up in its dancing that it sometimes doesn’t hear its Trainer’s orders.
descriptions.desc_741_2683: This Oricorio has sipped purple nectar. Some dancers use its graceful, elegant dancing as inspiration.
descriptions.desc_742: Cutiefly can pick up the auras of living things. It skillfully reads those auras to predict its foes' movements and make fools of them.
descriptions.desc_743: It can predict the weather from moisture levels and wind direction. Ribombee only reveals itself when there are a few clear days in a row.
descriptions.desc_744: When it rubs the rocks on its neck against you, that's proof of its love for you. However, the rocks are sharp, so the gesture is quite painful!
descriptions.desc_745: The rocks in its mane are sharper than a knife. Fragments that break off are treasured as good luck charms.
descriptions.desc_745_2684: The rocks in its mane are sharper than a knife. Fragments that break off are treasured as good luck charms.
descriptions.desc_745_2685: It has no problem ignoring orders it doesn’t like. It doesn’t seem to mind getting hurt at all—as long as it can finish off its opponent.
descriptions.desc_745_2686: This strange form is the result of its evolving at dusk. It’s very rare in Alola.
descriptions.desc_746: When it's in a jam, its shining eyes attract others of its kind. The light from its eyes is visible almost 25 miles away.
descriptions.desc_747: Aside from its head, its body parts regenerate quickly if they're cut off. After a good night's sleep, Mareanie is back to normal.
descriptions.desc_748: With its 12 legs, it creates a dome to shelter within. The flow of the tides doesn't affect Toxapex in there, so it's very comfortable.
descriptions.desc_749: Possessing mighty power, Mudbray can be loaded with 50 times its own body weight and will be totally fine.
descriptions.desc_750: It can trudge mountain roads without rest for three days and three nights, all the while dragging a 10-ton load.
descriptions.desc_751: It can only breathe oxygen that has dissolved in water, so it wears a water bubble on its head when it walks around on land.
descriptions.desc_752: It has a habit of storing things it values in its water bubble. If its Trainer doesn't watch out, Araquanid will try to put them in its bubble!
descriptions.desc_753: It loves the sunshine. When it basks in the sunlight regularly, it grows up with vivid coloration.
descriptions.desc_754: As it slashes into its enemies, it looks like it's dancing. Its elegant appearance has led some to call it the most glamorous Grass Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_755: It likes damp dark places. When night falls, the spores filling the caps of its mushrooms glow.
descriptions.desc_756: When it starts fighting for territory with Parasect, the entire area gets completely coated in spores!
descriptions.desc_757: It weakens opponents and sends them reeling with its poisonous gas. Salandit doesn't deal well with Spinda, since it's always reeling.
descriptions.desc_758: It punishes Salandit that couldn't bring it food with a fierce slap of its flame-spewing palm.
descriptions.desc_759: Stufful hates to be hugged or touched in any way. It will squirm, thrash, and resist with amazing power.
descriptions.desc_760: It boasts tremendous physical strength. Many people call it the most dangerous Pokémon in the Alola region.
descriptions.desc_761: It tries to resist being swallowed by a bird Pokémon by spinning the sepals on its head. It's usually a fruitless attempt.
descriptions.desc_762: It bounces around, swinging the sepals on its head with abandon. They're quite painful when they smack you!
descriptions.desc_763: A Pokémon with an aggressive personality and a mastery of kicking, it cackles every time it kicks an opponent.
descriptions.desc_764: It picks flowers and sticks them to its body with fluids it produces. The aroma that wafts from its petals has a healing effect.
descriptions.desc_765: Oranguru don't get along with each other, so they're always engaging in battles of wits to decide which one is superior.
descriptions.desc_766: Berries are its weapons as well as the staple of its diet. The one that can throw a berry the farthest is the boss of the troop.
descriptions.desc_767: An astonishingly cowardly Pokémon, Wimpod will whir its legs at high speeds to run away if anything comes near it.
descriptions.desc_768: Its claws, which it can extend and retract at will, are its greatest weapons. Golisopod is sometimes accompanied by Wimpod.
descriptions.desc_769: If you build sand mounds when you're playing, destroy them before you go home, or they may get possessed and become Sandygast.
descriptions.desc_770: Once it has whipped up a sandstorm to halt its opponents in their tracks, this terrifying Pokémon snatches away their vitality.
descriptions.desc_771: Its entire body is covered in its own slime. If you accidentally step on one, you'll slip, and it will get mad and smack you!
descriptions.desc_772: There's danger of its going on a rampage, so its true power is sealed away beneath its control mask.
descriptions.desc_773: Through the bond it formed with its Trainer, its will was strengthened, and it was able to destroy its control mask.
descriptions.desc_774: Although its outer shell is uncommonly durable, the shock of falling to the ground smashes the shell to smithereens.
descriptions.desc_775: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.
descriptions.desc_776: Its exploding shell poses a real danger but is sensitive to moisture. On rainy days, Turtonator takes silent refuge in caves.
descriptions.desc_777: Its capacity to produce electricity is somewhat limited, so it gets charged up by letting lightning strike it!
descriptions.desc_778: A gust of wind revealed what hides under this Pokémon's rag to a passing Trainer, who went home and died painfully that very night.
descriptions.desc_779: Its skin is thick enough to fend off Mareanie's spikes. With its robust teeth, Bruxish crunches up the spikes and eats them.
descriptions.desc_780: It appears in towns and plays with the children. Drampa will protect kids when they're in danger, so their moms don't have to worry.
descriptions.desc_781: Its chain-like green seaweed can stretch outward for hundreds of yards. For some reason, it gets along well with Skrelp.
descriptions.desc_782: It will never show an enemy its back in battle. Ancient warriors liked Jangmo-o for its valiant disposition and made it one of their own.
descriptions.desc_783: The scales it sheds can be molded and processed to make pots and pans. They conduct heat well, so they're a popular item.
descriptions.desc_784: It battles valiantly with its fists, which are armored in steel scales. Kommo-o specializes in uppercuts.
descriptions.desc_785: The lightning-wielding guardian deity of Melemele, Tapu Koko is brimming with curiosity and appears before people from time to time.
descriptions.desc_786: Although called a guardian deity, Tapu Lele is devoid of guilt about its cruel disposition and can be described as nature incarnate.
descriptions.desc_787: It makes ringing sounds with its tail to let others know where it is, avoiding unneeded conflicts. This guardian deity of Ula'ula controls plants.
descriptions.desc_788: Although it's called a guardian deity, terrible calamities sometimes befall those who recklessly approach Tapu Fini.
descriptions.desc_789: Whether or not it's a Pokémon from this world is a mystery. When it's in a jam, it warps away to a safe place to hide.
descriptions.desc_790: As it absorbs light, Cosmoem continues to grow. Its golden shell is surprisingly solid.
descriptions.desc_791: In writings from the distant past, it's called by the name “the beast that devours the sun.”
descriptions.desc_792: It sometimes summons unknown powers and life-forms here to this world from holes that lead to other worlds.
descriptions.desc_793: It appeared in this world from an Ultra Wormhole. Nihilego appears to be a parasite that lives by feeding on people and Pokémon.
descriptions.desc_794: Buzzwole goes around showing off its abnormally swollen muscles. It is one kind of Ultra Beast.
descriptions.desc_795: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.
descriptions.desc_796: They've been dubbed Ultra Beasts. Some of them stand unmoving, like trees, with their arms and legs stuck into the ground.
descriptions.desc_797: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.
descriptions.desc_798: This Ultra Beast's body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.
descriptions.desc_799: An unknown life-form called a UB. It may be constantly hungry—it is certainly always devouring something.
descriptions.desc_800: Light is the source of its energy. If it isn't devouring light, impurities build up in it and on it, and Necrozma darkens and stops moving.
descriptions.desc_800_2718: This is its form while it is devouring the light of Solgaleo. It pounces on foes and then slashes them with the claws on its four limbs and back.
descriptions.desc_800_2719: This is its form while it’s devouring the light of Lunala. It grasps foes in its giant claws and rips them apart with brute force.
descriptions.desc_801: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.
descriptions.desc_802: It sinks into the shadows of people and Pokémon, where it can understand their feelings and copy their capabilities.
descriptions.desc_803: An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.
descriptions.desc_804: One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.
descriptions.desc_805: When stone walls started moving and attacking, the brute's true identity was this mysterious life-form, which brings to mind an Ultra Beast.
descriptions.desc_806: A UB that appeared from an Ultra Wormhole, it causes explosions, then takes advantage of opponents' surprise to rob them of their vitality.
descriptions.desc_807: It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.
descriptions.desc_808: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.
descriptions.desc_809: Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.
descriptions.desc_810: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.
descriptions.desc_811: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.
descriptions.desc_812: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.
descriptions.desc_813: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon's body. Once that happens, it's ready to fight at full power.
descriptions.desc_814: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.
descriptions.desc_815: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.
descriptions.desc_816: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won't be able to resist weeping.
descriptions.desc_817: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.
descriptions.desc_818: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.
descriptions.desc_819: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.
descriptions.desc_820: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn't notice the loss.
descriptions.desc_821: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.
descriptions.desc_822: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.
descriptions.desc_823: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.
descriptions.desc_824: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn't.
descriptions.desc_825: It barely moves, but it's still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.
descriptions.desc_826: It's famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.
descriptions.desc_827: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.
descriptions.desc_828: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.
descriptions.desc_829: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.
descriptions.desc_830: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.
descriptions.desc_831: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.
descriptions.desc_832: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You'll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.
descriptions.desc_833: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.
descriptions.desc_834: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.
descriptions.desc_835: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.
descriptions.desc_836: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.
descriptions.desc_837: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.
descriptions.desc_838: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.
descriptions.desc_839: It's usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_840: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more.
descriptions.desc_841: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.
descriptions.desc_842: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.
descriptions.desc_843: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.
descriptions.desc_844: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.
descriptions.desc_845: It's so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it's battling midfight.
descriptions.desc_846: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It's very proud of that jaw.
descriptions.desc_847: This Pokémon has a jaw that's as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda's flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.
descriptions.desc_848: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.
descriptions.desc_849: When this Pokémon sounds as if it's strumming a guitar, it's actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.
descriptions.desc_849_2463: Capable of generating 15,000 volts of electricity, this Pokémon looks down on all that would challenge it.
descriptions.desc_849_2464: When this Pokémon sounds as if it's strumming a guitar, it's actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.
descriptions.desc_850: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.
descriptions.desc_851: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.
descriptions.desc_852: It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.
descriptions.desc_853: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.
descriptions.desc_854: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.
descriptions.desc_854_2477: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.
descriptions.desc_854_2478: The swirl pattern in this Pokémon's body is its weakness. If it gets stirred, the swirl loses its shape, and Sinistea gets dizzy.
descriptions.desc_855: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.
descriptions.desc_855_2480: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.
descriptions.desc_855_2481: Trainers Polteageist trusts will be allowed to experience its distinctive flavor and aroma firsthand by sampling just a tiny bit of its tea.
descriptions.desc_856: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures' emotions. If you don't have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.
descriptions.desc_857: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.
descriptions.desc_858: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.
descriptions.desc_859: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.
descriptions.desc_860: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it's trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.
descriptions.desc_861: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.
descriptions.desc_862: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.
descriptions.desc_863: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.
descriptions.desc_864: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon's core spirit.
descriptions.desc_865: Only Farfetch'd that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon's leek withers, it will retire from combat.
descriptions.desc_866: It's highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.
descriptions.desc_867: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.
descriptions.desc_868: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.
descriptions.desc_869: When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it's decorated with cream.
descriptions.desc_870: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass's orders are absolute.
descriptions.desc_871: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.
descriptions.desc_872: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.
descriptions.desc_873: Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit.
descriptions.desc_874: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.
descriptions.desc_875: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.
descriptions.desc_876: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.
descriptions.desc_877: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It's also generating electricity.
descriptions.desc_878: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It's also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.
descriptions.desc_879: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.
descriptions.desc_880: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.
descriptions.desc_881: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.
descriptions.desc_882: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.
descriptions.desc_883: Though it's able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.
descriptions.desc_884: Its body resembles polished metal, and it's both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.
descriptions.desc_885: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.
descriptions.desc_886: It's capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.
